column1: # scripts/schema-check/ledger-reconciliation.tsv
# THE RECORD of how every row of production's migration ledger,
# supabase_migrations.schema_migrations, lines up with supabase/migrations/.
# Issue #91. Read reconcile-ledger.js for the mechanism, the export query and
# the verdict vocabulary; run `node scripts/schema-check/reconcile-ledger.js
# check` (also run by reconcile-ledger.test.ts under `npm test`) to hold this
# file against the repo.
# Columns, tab-separated: version  name  verdict  file  note
#   version  the ledger's version string: 14 digits for a run through the MCP
#            server or the CLI, 0XX for a CLI push of a numbered file, `?` for
#            a row known by name only (named on #78 or in a file header) whose
#            version the export has not supplied yet, `-` for a repo file row.
#   name     the ledger's name column; `?` when only the version is known.
#   verdict  tracked | recovered-by | consolidated-by | number-collision |
#            missing-file | no-ledger-row (defined in reconcile-ledger.js).
#   file     the supabase/migrations file the verdict names, if any.
#   note     evidence, by file:line where it lives in the repo.
# STATUS 2026-10-16. The full export has not been produced: it needs a
# connection to production, which @slowdog-dev used for the #78 findings and
# which this record's author did not have. Every row below is what the repo
# and the #78 thread establish on their own. Rows with `?` are the ones the
# export settles; `import` fills the version in by name and appends every row
# it does not know. Until then:
#   * The #78 thread names roughly 25 rows between 004 and 031 with 14-digit
#     versions. The ones keyed below are those the repo and the thread
#     establish; `?` marks a version the export has not supplied. The 008 and
#     009 batches alone account for several more: 008:4-6 cites versions
#     through 20260805181547, two overlapping MCP sessions on 2026-08-05 whose
#     per-row names are unknown. The check classifies any version inside
#     either range as consolidated-by that file.
#   * 023:1-9 says the check_post_rate_limit auth.uid() check was "applied
#     directly to the live database" on 2026-08-19 and captured in 023 later.
#     That is a row with neither version nor name known, so it has no line
#     here; the export will surface it as missing-file and the verdict to
#     record is `tracked 023_...`, with the version cited in 023's header.
#   * Outside the ledger entirely: the `avatars` storage bucket was created in
#     the dashboard and has neither a ledger row nor a file (030:101-103).
#     Not a ledger reconciliation item, recorded here so nobody looks for it.
# Nothing in this file is a migration. Writing a migration for a missing-file
# row needs that row's `statements` column, which only the export carries.
